## Data import, parsing & cleaning

We start by loading the required libraries.

```{r, echo=TRUE}
# Load required libraries
library(ismev)
library(tidyverse)
library(knitr)
library(kableExtra)
```

Next, we fetch data from our chosen river gauging station, *Don at Parkhill* in Scotland. For 10 years of 15-minute interval data, we are fetching over 350,000 records. To minimse the chances of a 504 Gateway Timeout, we will fetch the data in 1-year blocks and save it to our local disk so future runs do not have to re-download the data.

```{r, echo=TRUE}
# Extend R's default HTTP timeout limit to 300 seconds
options(timeout = 300)

cache_file <- "river_don_parkhill_flow.rds"

if (file.exists(cache_file)) {
  # Load from local cache if file already exists
  river_data <- readRDS(cache_file)
  
} else {
  # If no local cache exists, fetch from SEPA in 1-year chunks
  start_years <- seq(2016, 2025, by = 1)
  
  fetch_chunk <- function(yr) {
    from_date <- paste0(yr, "-08-31T00:00:00")
    to_date   <- paste0(yr + 1, "-08-31T00:00:00")
    
    url <- paste0(
      "https://timeseries.sepa.org.uk/KiWIS/KiWIS?",
      "service=kisters&type=queryServices&datasource=0&",
      "request=getTimeseriesValues&ts_path=1/234292/Q/15m.Cmd&",
      "from=", from_date, "&to=", to_date, "&",
      "metadata=true&returnfields=Timestamp,Value,Quality%20Code&format=csv"
    )
    
    read_delim(
      url, 
      delim = ";", 
      comment = "#",
      col_names = c("Timestamp", "Discharge", "QualityCode"),
      show_col_types = FALSE
    )
  }
  
  river_data <- map_dfr(start_years, fetch_chunk) %>%
    mutate(Timestamp = as.POSIXct(Timestamp, format = "%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S")) %>%
    filter(!is.na(Discharge)) %>%
    distinct(Timestamp, .keep_all = TRUE)
  
  # Save to local file so future runs don't need to use the API
  saveRDS(river_data, cache_file)
}
```

Shifting our attention to the `QualityCode` column, let us assess the data segmented by quality code.

```{r, echo=FALSE}
# Create the quality code table from SEPA guidance
quality_code_table <- tibble(
  `Code number` = c(50, 100, 140, 150, 200, 254),
  `Code name` = c(
    "Good", 
    "Estimated", 
    "Provisional", 
    "Suspect", 
    "Unchecked<br>(imported from legacy database)", 
    "Unchecked"
  ),
  `Abbreviated code name` = c("G", "E", "Prov", "S", "V", "U")
)

# Generate table
quality_code_table %>%
  kable(
    format = "html", 
    escape = FALSE, 
    caption = "Table 1 — quality codes",
    align = c("c", "l", "c") # c = center, l = left
  ) %>%
  kable_styling(
    bootstrap_options = c("bordered", "striped", "hover"), 
    full_width = FALSE,
    position = "left"
  )
```

```{r, echo=TRUE}
# Segment data by QualityCode split
quality_summary <- river_data %>%
  count(QualityCode) %>%
  mutate(
    Percentage = sprintf("%.2f%%", (n / sum(n)) * 100)
  )

print(quality_summary)
```

We observe that the majority of the data is "Good" by SEPA's quality control standards. Given that only 0.01% of the data is "Unchecked", we remove these entries from the data set to ensure all of the data we use in our analysis has been quality checked.

```{r}
# Remove rows where QualityCode is 254
river_data <- river_data %>%
  filter(QualityCode != 254)

# Produce new data segmentation by QualityCode split
quality_summary <- river_data %>%
  count(QualityCode) %>%
  mutate(
    Percentage = sprintf("%.2f%%", (n / sum(n)) * 100)
  )

print(quality_summary)
```

Next, 4.10% of the data is assigned quality code 100, meaning they are estimated. Many of the peaks we will observe are estimated, but we cannot remove these for now given these are the extreme values we are studying.

## Threshold selection for Peaks Over Threshold method

To choose a defensible threshold $u$, we start by comparing standard empirical benchmarks such as setting a threshold yielding an average of 3-5 peaks per year or selecting the 95th percentile of discharge values.

Selecting $u_{3-5}$:

```{r, echo=TRUE}
# Calculate length of the dataset in years
n_years <- as.numeric(difftime(max(river_data$Timestamp), 
                               min(river_data$Timestamp), 
                               units = "days")) / 365.25

# Counts independent peak events for a given candidate threshold u
get_annual_peak_rate <- function(u, data, n_yrs, min_gap_hours = 72) {
  
  # Filter observations above candidate threshold u
  exceedances <- data %>% 
    filter(Discharge > u) %>%
    arrange(Timestamp)
  
  if (nrow(exceedances) == 0) return(0)
  
  # Flag new independent event if time since last exceedance > min_gap_hours
  exceedances <- exceedances %>%
    mutate(
      time_gap = as.numeric(difftime(Timestamp, lag(Timestamp, default = Timestamp[5]), units = "hours")),
      new_event = ifelse(time_gap > min_gap_hours | row_number() == 1, 1, 0),
      event_id = cumsum(new_event)
    )
  
  # Calculate number of unique peak events
  n_peaks <- max(exceedances$event_id)
  
  return(n_peaks / n_yrs)
}

# Grid search over candidate discharge thresholds
u_grid <- seq(quantile(river_data$Discharge, 0.80), 
              quantile(river_data$Discharge, 0.99), 
              length.out = 100)

# Calculate annual peak rate for each threshold in the grid
rate_results <- tibble(u = u_grid) %>%
  mutate(peaks_per_year = map_dbl(u, ~get_annual_peak_rate(.x, river_data, n_years)))

# Extract thresholds corresponding to target rates (e.g., 3, 4, and 5 peaks/year)
u_target_3 <- rate_results %>% filter(peaks_per_year <= 3) %>% pull(u) %>% first()
u_target_4 <- rate_results %>% filter(peaks_per_year <= 4) %>% pull(u) %>% first()
u_target_5 <- rate_results %>% filter(peaks_per_year <= 5) %>% pull(u) %>% first()

cat("Threshold for ~5 peaks/year:", round(u_target_5, 2), "m^3/s\n")
cat("Threshold for ~4 peaks/year:", round(u_target_4, 2), "m^3/s\n")
cat("Threshold for ~3 peaks/year:", round(u_target_3, 2), "m^3/s\n")
```

Selecting $u_{95}$:

```{r, echo=TRUE}
# Compute 95th percentile threshold
u_95 <- quantile(river_data$Discharge, probs = 0.95, na.rm = TRUE)

cat("95th Percentile Threshold", round(u_95, 2), "m^3/s\n")
cat("Total record length:", round(n_years, 2), "years\n")
```

Now we turn our attention to using asymptotic theory to justify a selection of a threshold, $u$. Since the 95th Percentile Threshold is less than the threshold for 5 peaks/year, we choose $u_{emp} = u_3$ where $u_3$ is the threshold for 3 peaks per year.

```{r, echo=TRUE}
u_emp <- u_target_3
```

Calculating the average time to rise from 5 clean peaks:

```{r, echo=TRUE}
# Identify continuous exceedance clusters above u_emp
exceedance_clusters <- river_data %>%
  mutate(above_u = Discharge > u_emp) %>%
  mutate(cluster_id = cumsum(above_u != lag(above_u, default = FALSE) & above_u)) %>%
  filter(above_u)

# Select top 5 largest distinct hydrograph crests
top_5_peaks <- exceedance_clusters %>%
  group_by(cluster_id) %>%
  slice_max(Discharge, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  arrange(desc(Discharge)) %>%
  slice(1:5) %>%
  arrange(Timestamp)

# Measure duration between preceding trough and peak crest
t_rise_list <- numeric(nrow(top_5_peaks))

for (i in seq_len(nrow(top_5_peaks))) {
  peak_time <- top_5_peaks$Timestamp[i]
  window_start <- peak_time - (5 * 24 * 3600) # Look back 5 days for trough
  
  preceding_window <- river_data %>%
    filter(Timestamp >= window_start & Timestamp <= peak_time)
  
  trough_time <- preceding_window %>%
    filter(Discharge == min(Discharge)) %>%
    pull(Timestamp) %>%
    min()
  
  t_rise_list[i] <- as.numeric(difftime(peak_time, trough_time, units = "hours"))
}

# Append t_rise_list as a new column to top_5_peaks
top_5_peaks <- top_5_peaks %>%
  mutate(t_rise_hours = t_rise_list)

t_rise_avg_hours <- mean(t_rise_list)
min_sep_hours <- 3 * t_rise_avg_hours # Robson & Reed rule: 3 * T_rise

cat("Measured T_rise for 5 clean peaks (hrs):", round(t_rise_list, 1), "\n")
cat("Mean T_rise:", round(t_rise_avg_hours, 1), "hours\n")
cat("Min Time Separation Criterion (3 * T_rise):", round(min_sep_hours, 1), "hours\n")
```

Implementing the Robson & Reed independence criteria:

```{r, echo=TRUE}
decluster_robson_reed <- function(data, u, min_sep_hrs, trough_drop_ratio = 2/3) {
  
  exceed_data <- data %>%
    mutate(above_u = Discharge > u) %>%
    mutate(cluster_id = cumsum(above_u != lag(above_u, default = FALSE) & above_u)) %>%
    filter(above_u)
  
  if (nrow(exceed_data) == 0) return(tibble())
  
  cluster_peaks <- exceed_data %>%
    group_by(cluster_id) %>%
    slice_max(Discharge, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE) %>%
    ungroup() %>%
    arrange(Timestamp)
  
  independent_peaks <- list()
  
  for (i in seq_len(nrow(cluster_peaks))) {
    if (length(independent_peaks) == 0) {
      independent_peaks[[4]] <- cluster_peaks[i, ]
    } else {
      prev_peak <- independent_peaks[[length(independent_peaks)]]
      curr_peak <- cluster_peaks[i, ]
      
      # Robson & Reed: Time interval between two adjacent peaks >= 3 * average time to rise
      time_gap_hrs <- as.numeric(difftime(curr_peak$Timestamp, prev_peak$Timestamp, units = "hours"))
      
      # Inter-peak trough discharge <= (1 - 2/3) * previous peak
      trough_data <- data %>%
        filter(Timestamp >= prev_peak$Timestamp & Timestamp <= curr_peak$Timestamp)
      
      min_trough_discharge <- min(trough_data$Discharge, na.rm = TRUE)
      
      time_valid <- time_gap_hrs >= min_sep_hrs
      drop_valid <- min_trough_discharge <= (1 - trough_drop_ratio) * prev_peak$Discharge
      
      if (time_valid && drop_valid) {
        independent_peaks[[length(independent_peaks) + 1]] <- curr_peak
      }
    }
  }
  
  bind_rows(independent_peaks)
}

# Run declustering
declustered_events <- decluster_robson_reed(
  data = river_data, 
  u = u_emp, 
  min_sep_hrs = min_sep_hours, 
  trough_drop_ratio = 2/3
)

cat("Total independent peak events identified:", nrow(declustered_events), "\n")
cat("Final annual rate:", round(nrow(declustered_events) / n_years, 2), "peaks/year\n")
```

Plotting the ismev asymptotic diagnostics:

```{r, echo=TRUE}
# Convert declustered peak magnitudes to 1D numeric vector for ismev
peak_vector <- declustered_events$Discharge

# Mean Residual Life (MRL) Plot
mrl.plot(peak_vector)

# Parameter Stability Plot
gpd.fitrange(peak_vector, umin = 50, umax = 150)
```

```{r, echo=TRUE}
gpd_fit <- gpd.fit(peak_vector, 90)
gpd.diag(gpd_fit)
```
